title: Kalaignar Karunanidhi and the Budget Debate: Human Compassion Over Cold Balance Sheets
summary: When fiscal orthodoxies challenged his revolutionary social welfare programs, Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi argued that a state budget must serve human dignity above dry accounting numbers.
full_text:
In the early 1970s, during annual budget deliberations at the Tamil Nadu secretariat, Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi announced an ambitious social welfare initiative: the complete abolition of hand-pulled rickshaws across the state and the free distribution of motorized cycle-rickshaws to all pullers.

Finance department officials raised orthodox fiscal objections:
"Honorable Chief Minister, procuring tens of thousands of cycle rickshaws will impose a massive burden on the state exchequer. Economists may classify this expenditure as non-productive social welfare rather than capital infrastructure investment."

Karunanidhi listened, laid his fountain pen upon the desk, and addressed the treasury officials:
"Gentlemen, a budget is not an arid mathematical ledger designed solely to balance debit and credit columns. Can any civilized society tolerate a practice where one human being is yoked like a beast of burden to pull another?
Is the restoration of human dignity to forty thousand impoverished families not the highest and most productive capital investment a democratic state can make?

The virtue of a government is not measured by the surplus it hoards in treasury vaults, but by the tears of humiliation it wipes away! The true profit of our budget lies in the radiant self-respect of the working poor."

The initiative was enacted into law, eradicating hand-pulled rickshaws from Tamil Nadu. Karunanidhi established that economic policy must be the servant of human compassion and social justice.
